extracted.intended_audience: agency rule-makers, agency staff, regulatory attorneys, participants in federal rulemaking, and others interested in administrative law
extracted.subtask_description: A stage-by-stage practical guide to informal federal agency rulemaking, covering statutory provisions, procedural requirements, public participation, administrative recordkeeping, judicial review, and post-promulgation responsibilities. Intended to help agency officials and participants comply with procedural and substantive obligations in U.S. federal rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of federal agency rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: A general, stage-by-stage view of the federal rulemaking process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces the full rulemaking lifecycle to orient agency rule-makers and participants; frames subsequent procedural and substantive requirements discussed in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Administrative Procedure Act's rulemaking provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA provisions that govern rulemaking, especially standards for informal rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers statutory requirements under the APA that agencies must follow when promulgating rules (notice-and-comment procedures, substantive constraints, etc.). The guide focuses on informal rather than formal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rulemaking or adjudication for the setting of policy: a comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: How to choose between rulemaking and adjudication for establishing policy and the comparative advantages/constraints of each route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains criteria and tradeoffs agencies should evaluate when deciding whether to use rulemaking or adjudication to set policy; discusses procedural and legal consequences of the choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other procedural statutes affecting rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-APA statutes and statutory requirements that also affect agency rulemaking procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies additional procedural obligations imposed by statutes beyond the APA (e.g., notice, hearings, consultation, special procedures) and how they interact with APA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginning the process
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and practical steps an agency should take at the outset of rule development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses planning, internal decisionmaking, advance notice mechanisms, delegation of authority, and initial legal and policy analysis necessary before publishing a proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of electronic tools and platforms (e.g., regulations.gov) for notice, comment, and recordkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on best practices and legal considerations for using electronic submission and docketing systems, including public access, comment management, and compliance with e-rulemaking requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory analysis and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical requirements and review processes (e.g., regulatory impact analysis, cost-benefit assessment) that inform and justify rulemaking decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when regulatory analysis is required, standards for economic and other analyses, executive branch review procedures (OMB review, interagency review), and how analyses affect rule content and defensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: The notice of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and content expectations for the NPRM (notice of proposed rulemaking) published to solicit public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details what must appear in a lawful NPRM (statement of need, legal basis, proposed text, request for comment), how to craft adequate notices to satisfy APA notice-and-comment requirements, and common pitfalls that lead to judicial invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms, standards, and practical guidance for securing and considering public comments and participation in rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers who may participate, how agencies should solicit and treat comments, meaningful participation standards, and best practices to ensure the administrative record reflects meaningful engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: The rulemaking record
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and practices for creating, maintaining, and using the administrative record that supports agency rulemaking decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the components of a complete rulemaking record, evidentiary and documentation practices, how to assemble an adequate record to support decisionmaking and judicial review, and strategies to avoid record deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Off-the-record" or "ex parte" communications in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and limits governing off-the-record and ex parte contacts with decisionmakers during rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes prohibitions, disclosure requirements, permissible communications, and procedures to address or document ex parte contacts to preserve fairness and avoid legal challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: The final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for issuing a final rule, including responding to comments, revisions to proposals, and drafting final regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on how to explain changes from the NPRM, respond to significant comments, ensure reasoned decisionmaking, and produce a legally defensible final rule that reflects appropriate consideration of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibilities after the rule is issued
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-promulgation duties such as publication, compliance monitoring, guidance, and implementation actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses publication in the Federal Register, effective dates, implementation planning, interpretive guidance, monitoring and enforcement responsibilities, and recordkeeping after issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how agency rulemaking decisions are subject to judicial review and the legal bases for challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains doctrines that allow or bar judicial review of rulemaking actions, timing and venue for challenges, and common grounds for review (statutory, constitutional, procedural).

rubrics_metrics.name: The scope of judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards courts apply when reviewing agency rules (e.g., arbitrary and capricious, substantial evidence, Chevron deference issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the legal standards and remedial possibilities courts use to evaluate the sufficiency of agency reasoning, record support, statutory interpretation, and whether agency action should be set aside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review of agency failure to act
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedures for suing an agency for unreasonable delay or failure to promulgate required rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers legal mechanisms (e.g., mandamus, APA suits to compel action), standards for unreasonable delay, and strategic considerations when seeking judicial relief for agency inaction.
